minutes.headline: Planning Board approved a 30 Gilchrist St ANR plan and continued the site plan rules hearing to March 22.
minutes.summary: The board endorsed an approval-not-required plan creating two new house lots at the Northfield pool property, then continued the public hearing on site plan and special permit rules so two wording changes could be advertised. In a workshop it reworked the draft parking bylaw table for the spring Town Meeting warrant, and agreed to restore a lost two-family lot-size requirement. Members also pressed to shift attention to master planning and Town facilities, and appointed a member to the Economic Development Committee.

votes.motion: Approve the ANR plan for 30 Gilchrist Street, with a copy of the signed Board of Health endorsement placed in the file
Continue the site plan and special permit rules and regulations public hearing to March 22 at 6:35 pm
Appoint Mary Ray Holman to the Economic Development Committee on the Agricultural Commission's recommendation

budget_items.what_was_said: A member asked why the fee structure adopted in 2006 has not been revised. The planner said it could be updated and offered to bring a comparison with other communities.

A member recalled Town Meeting appropriated money for a cost estimate and noted spending on engineering with no tangible output. The committee reported the renovation estimate exceeds a teardown and rebuild, and nobody is comfortable recommending the estimated amount.

decisions.decision: Board agreed the tennis court setback and lot access were the applicant's risk and not grounds to deny the ANR.
Planner to draft wording changes (minor drainage changes; stormwater language matching the bylaw) and post them on the website before the continued hearing.
Parking table edits agreed: drop 'sleeping' from private camp, add day care, restaurant seat ratio, separate conference space, marijuana retail/dispensary category, B&B non-resident employee.
Planner to bring camp and restaurant carryout parking comparisons from Lancaster, Littleton and Harvard to the next meeting.
Board agreed to aim to submit the parking bylaw for the spring Annual Town Meeting warrant, with floor amendment possible.
Planner to draft a warrant article restoring the 1.5 times lot size requirement for two-family dwellings.
Subdivision procedure revisions back-burnered in favour of master plan work.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted 4-0 to approve an approval-not-required plan creating two house lots at 30 Gilchrist Street.
The board voted 4-0 to continue the site plan and special permit rules hearing to March 22 so two wording changes can be posted and advertised.
In a workshop the board edited the draft parking bylaw table and agreed to aim for the spring Annual Town Meeting warrant, with a floor amendment possible.
The planner was asked to draft a warrant article restoring the 1.5 times lot size requirement for two-family dwellings.
The board voted 4-0 to appoint a member to the Economic Development Committee on the Agricultural Commission's recommendation.

why_it_matters: The parking table and the two-family lot size article are zoning changes headed for the spring Town Meeting warrant, where residents will be asked to vote on them.
Two new house lots at the Gilchrist Street property were endorsed without a hearing, since approval-not-required plans go through the board without a public hearing.
watch_next: March 22 at 6:35 pm: continued public hearing on the site plan and special permit rules, with the drainage and stormwater wording posted beforehand.
The next meeting: the planner's parking comparisons from Lancaster, Littleton and Harvard for camps and restaurant carryout.
